title: share account OHK-SHARE-ACCT purchase: 137 shares at 137.50 MNT = 18837.50 (non-round money)
_note: share-account seam, ACCOUNT DETAIL READ-BACK, and the corpus's first NON-ROUND purchase price and share counts. request.purchased_price "137.50" is share-account-detail-raw.json purchasedShares[0].purchasedPrice, the exact 2dp decimal text the oracle stored; expect.purchased_price_minor "13750" is that same value in integer minor units (2dp). request.purchased_amount "18837.50" is purchasedShares[0].amount and expect.purchased_amount_minor "1883750" its minor-unit form: the purchase total is requestedShares 137 * unitPrice 137.50 = 18837.50, exact at 2dp, so NO sub-minor residue exists (G-19 / DEC-2 G-08). request.total_approved_shares 137 and request.purchased_shares 137 are summary.totalApprovedShares and purchasedShares[0].numberOfShares; 1373 = 137 * 10 + 3, so the count does not divide the product total. request.total_pending_shares 0 and expect.total_pending_shares 0 are summary.totalPendingForApprovalShares. request.account_status_id 300 and expect.account_status_stored 300 are status.id (shareAccountStatusType.active). request.purchased_status_id 300 and expect.purchased_status_stored 300 are purchasedShares[0].status.id (purchasedSharesStatusType.approved). The seed corpus fixes purchased_price at 100.00 and the counts at 100/1000 on every vector, so a port that hardcodes the price or the share count is invisible elsewhere; 137.50 and 137 make those defects go red here.
